summary: Adds the BGP communities attribute, a tag that can be attached to routes so neighboring and distant networks can group them and apply policy to the whole group. It gives operators a simple way to signal their routing wishes.

plainLanguage.summary: Sticky labels on parcels let the post office handle every parcel with the same label the same way. BGP communities are labels on routes.

questions: what is the bgp communities attribute type code
subtitle: A tag on BGP routes that lets operators group destinations and apply policy to the whole group.

tldr.problem: BGP policy was controlled only by IP prefixes or the AS_PATH attribute, which made configuration large and hard to maintain.
tldr.mechanism: The COMMUNITIES path attribute (type code 8) carries a set of 32-bit community values, so policy can match a group identity instead.
tldr.outcome: It also defines the well-known values NO_EXPORT, NO_ADVERTISE and NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED. It has been updated by RFC 7606 and RFC 8642.

today: RFC 1997 is a Proposed Standard that was updated by RFC 7606 and RFC 8642.

sections.title: Grouping Destinations
sections.content:
BGP supports transit policy by controlling how routing information is distributed, but that control was based on IP address prefixes or the value of AS_PATH. This RFC suggests grouping destinations so decisions can also be based on a group identity. A community is a group of destinations sharing some common property, and every destination belongs by default to the general Internet community.

The examples show why: an NSFNET operator could tag acceptable-use compliant destinations instead of keeping a huge prefix and AS path filter database, and aggregate component prefixes could be tagged so they do not spread beyond their scope.
sections.plainLanguage: Put the same sticker on all the parcels that should be handled the same way, then give the rule just once.

sections.title: The COMMUNITIES Attribute
sections.content: The COMMUNITIES attribute is an optional transitive path attribute of variable length with Type Code 8. It is a set of four-octet values, and a route belongs to every community listed. Values 0x00000000 through 0x0000FFFF and 0xFFFF0000 through 0xFFFFFFFF are reserved. Other values carry an autonomous system number in the first two octets, and that AS defines the meaning of the last two.
sections.plainLanguage: Each label is a four-part code. The first half says who made the label, and the second half is whatever that maker wants it to mean.

sections.title: Well-known Communities and Operation
sections.content:
Three well-known communities must be implemented by any community-aware speaker. NO_EXPORT (0xFFFFFF01) means do not advertise outside a BGP confederation boundary. NO_ADVERTISE (0xFFFFFF02) means do not advertise to any other BGP peer. NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED (0xFFFFFF03) means do not advertise to external BGP peers.

A speaker may use the attribute to control what it accepts, prefers or distributes. It may add the attribute to a route that lacks it and may modify it by local policy. An aggregate without ATOMIC_AGGREGATE should carry all communities from the aggregated routes. The RFC says security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: Some stickers mean the same thing everywhere, like do not pass this on, and every post office must obey them.
